utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, we have Witness 49. Sir, would you please make the solemn declaration in the document which is being shown to you on the screen. I hope that it is being shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us your name, please?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Nezir Cengic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you were born?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: 1st February, 1914.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Cengic, in 1992, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Rataja, Miljevina municipality in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you working at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. How could I work? I was retired. I had my own livestock and chicken in the country, in my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you live with anyone or did you live alone?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I lived alone. I had two sons in Sarajevo, but I was there alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When the war in Foca started on the 8th of April, 1992, did that have an effect on you in Miljevina?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. We lived very nicely. We were born together there, us and Serbs. That was until the 17th of August. Then we were deprived of freedom, locked up, made to suffer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Before the 17th of August, could you see any destruction being caused by the war?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: How could I not see? Of course I saw it. Everyone was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you see nearby villages burning?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course I saw it. There are dozens of villages around. All of them were aflame. Everything that could burn, burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you give us the names of the villages that you saw burning?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Govza number 1, Govza number 2, Jelec, Drace, Poljice, Banjine, Izbisno, Mrdjanovici; all of them I saw burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: On the 17th of August, 1992, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I just went to feed my -- I was going to feed my cattle and give them water. A policeman stopped me in the yard. He deprived me of freedom and that's how I stayed with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did he say when he stopped you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: He didn't tell me anything. He just told me I was deprived of freedom, and all of us who were around, we were rounded up and taken to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How many people were rounded up with you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: From that village, we were -- we were five.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What ethnicity were the five of you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: All Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened when you were taken to the police station?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Everyone was taken there, and I was called out immediately and that soldier, what his rank was I don't know, he said, "Stand at attention," and then he hit me with his rifle on my back. I was 72 years old. I fainted. I started swearing at him, "How dare you beat me? If only my children found out about this." Then two of them started beating me, kicking me from both sides, and then I fainted again. When I came to, they were not there any more, and I joined the other four too in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The two who were beating you, were they both soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Some of them were in camouflage uniforms, Some of them were in olive-green/grey uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnicity those soldiers were who were beating you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: How could I know? I didn't dare say a word. They did whatever they pleased with us. They beat us. They beat me unconscious because probably somebody told them that I had money and valuables, but I wasn't saying a word because I thought if I say something, they're going to beat me again and ask for money.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did they say anything to you about your being Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't say anything, and we didn't say a word. They did whatever they wanted. They broke our bones, beat us, and so on. And then I was transferred to hospital. The others stayed at the KP Dom, the four of them, another couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Before we get to your transfer to the hospital, let's go back to when you were brought to join the other four people. Please give us the names of the other four people.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: There was Fehim Cengic, Sucro Softic. Both of them are dead now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And the names of the other two?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: There was Hilmo Cengic and Klino Mustafa.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were any of them related to you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: The Cengics were related to me and Klino wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you spend that night in the police station?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. And in the morning, they came to take me again. They took me to my home because they wanted gold coins and valuables and money, and they didn't take the others, just me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who took you back to your home?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Two soldiers. We got into a car, and they drove me to my home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did they do when you arrived at your home?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: What did they do? The house was opened. It stayed opened, and that's the way it was all night. Everybody took what they wanted. I told them, "You go in and take whatever you want." I gave them the money I had on me, and they said, "Don't tell anyone, because we'll cut your throat." I said I didn't know anything. I only had my shirt and my overcoat on and that's how I spent the night. If I were not a Muslim, I'd have paid them back, because Muslims are defended to do so by their faith, and I couldn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did the soldiers do --

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I would have killed myself.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologizes.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I would have killed myself if my faith allowed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After the soldiers took your money and things from your house, where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Again to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: While they took you, or on your way to the police station, did they say anything or do anything to you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: They took me to the police station. They called me out again and then they beat and beat me until I showed signs of life. Then I fainted. I don't know what else was going on. I was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Before that, did they put any item of clothing on you, like a hat?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. They put a cap on me, fez, and they told me to speak, but they told me to say on television what they wanted me to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there anything written on the fez?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Was there anything written? No, nothing was written on the fez. What could have been written?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know what the meaning was when they put the fez on your head?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: That I should say on television what they wanted me to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you go on television?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: On television, I didn't. I was in hospital for 50 days. I couldn't lie down because my ribs and my bones hurt. What do you mean, television?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said that they said you had to say what they wanted you to say on television, so my question was did you actually do that?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't take me. How could they have? Because I went to the hospital. I was beaten up silly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did they say what they wanted you to say on television? Or just everything that they told you that they would tell you to say?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. No, no. When they put this fez on me, they just said that I should repeat what they were saying after them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And what were they saying that you had to repeat?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you just said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said that after they put the fez on you, they told you to repeat what they were saying. What were they saying that you were asked to repeat? Did they say anything that they asked you to repeat?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did they say that you had to repeat?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: They were driving me in front of them. There was no television. They were taking me to Foca.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, we didn't hear the last sentence, the last part of what you said. Could you repeat it so the interpreters can hear you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I didn't get television. As soon as I got to the police station, and the same thing again; he called me out, they beat me, I fell on my back and they continued beating me until I showed signs of life. Then I was transferred to the hospital where I remained unconscious. That was in the hospital in Foca. Did you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, sir. Who told the soldiers to take you to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: My God. How can you ask that? I don't know who said what because I was unconscious. I had fainted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did one of your neighbours come to the police station?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Neighbours, what neighbours?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know Ilija Goljanin?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know Ilija Goljanin. That is my next-door neighbour. His father died, and he completed some course, he worked as a doctor. And once I told my neighbour to tell Ilija to come because I was beaten up. I don't remember whether I got together with the neighbour or with Ilija, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did that neighbour come to the police station and ask that you be taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't aware of anything. I was unconscious. Somebody came. I was unconscious. Somebody approached me. I said, "Please go away. I'm -- don't. I'm tired enough as it is. I'm 72 years old." Just a second. I'm 88 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What kind of treatment did you receive at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: It was a doctor who was treating me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot understand this. Can you please stop the witness here?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, the interpreter can't hear you at all. You have to start again, and please move closer to the microphone, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I am -- I have come closer now. I can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The question was: What kind of treatment did you receive at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: A lady doctor treated me. I got oxygen straight away and then I received tranquilisers. Then I got tea. It returned me back to life. I asked where I was. This woman who treated me, she stayed there until midnight and only then did she go home. She treated me for 10 or 15 days. Then a Chetnik came to the hospital, carrying a knife. He wanted to cut my throat. And then I had to go to the KP Dom at 10.00 p.m. at night because, otherwise, they would have killed me. There was no army to protect me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What day was it when this person came to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Oh, God, if only I could have brains enough to remember. I don't even know when. I didn't take any notes. I think it was in September, and which date it was, I don't know. It was September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say a Chetnik came, can you tell us what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Well, what else can I explain to you? They were treating us there, and he came to slit our throats. What else do you need to know? She was crying there, and he told her that he was fighting us. Fighting me? Eighty-eight years old, barely able to walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was the person you described as a Chetnik in uniform?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was wearing a soldier's uniform. He went there to visit his colleague. He was up there, fighting, and his cousin had -- was wounded. There were three other people there with me, they were incapacitated, and that was at the time when Foca fell. The doctor called the police and the police defended us. I tried -- they tried three times again that night, and they didn't let us stay in the hospital; we had to go to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you said that this person came with a knife and threatened to cut you, did he actually injure you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. He hit me with a chair, and he took off my shoulder blade from the right shoulder. I was in such pain. It was worse than if he had broken my arm. And the other one was beating with his fists. They must have both been mad or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say "the other one," was that person also in uniform?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: The other one. Did I say "the other one"? There was one Chetnik, and the doctor was doing her rounds, and she said he wanted to slit our throats. Then she called the police, started crying, and that's how it happened. The police came, and she, the doctor, didn't dare leave us there for the night. She had to -- we had to be sent to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you beaten by one person or by two people? I just wanted to clarify that because it sounded like there was some -- it wasn't clear to me.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: One person came. One Chetnik came to visit his comrade. He was only one, I never mentioned two.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he say anything while he beat you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: What do I know whether he was saying something? I don't even know what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he call you Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: It could have been. He could have called me Ustasha, I don't know. He could have called me anything. He was speaking -- talking to himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who took you to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: A car took us, and a driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said earlier that they tried three times to do something. Could you tell us what that was?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Three times he came to that room where we were to slit our throats and to beat us, but he was thrown out all three times. He didn't come there to visit me or bring me a present. He came there to kill me. And he almost did. It would have been better if they had killed me, better than this suffering I'm going through today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you arrived at the KP Dom, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I was taken to the place where my folks were, in that room.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What room was that? What floor was it in?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: How do I know? I wasn't counting floors. I wasn't interested. It was high up. And I got out, and they were -- they had been in an isolation cell from Miljevina. One of them was blind, one of them was a military invalid, and there were another two who were beaten. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say you were taken to the room where your folks were, what do you mean? Who else was there already?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: The one with whom I was taken away from my village. I've already told you. Why should I repeat this ten times? I already told who I was taken away with. We were taken to the police station, and they had stayed there while I was in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Are you talking, then, about the same four people who were at the police station in Miljevina with you? They were already at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had already arrived at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you said that they were in isolation cell before they were taken to that room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I don't know. They know better where they had been. They told me there was nothing there, it was a bare place, you just walk in. You have to sleep there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you were brought to this room, were there only these four people there or were there other people as well? Sir, were there other people in the room, aside from these four people?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: The four of them, no one else. I didn't hear the number. We who came from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the number, how many people came from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How many people came with you from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I can. Safet Mirzic and - what's his name? - Cocalic Ibro. He's an old man. He's already dead. He had gone for an exchange but he couldn't stand the journey and he died. I think Safet died, too, because he was very ill.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were those two people who were taken -- were those two people you just mentioned also being beaten at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, they were beaten too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Now, you started telling us -- you told us that of the four people who were already in that room, you said one of them was blind and one of them was a military invalid. Can you explain to us what you mean by --

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what you mean by "military invalid"?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: He was in the military and then he was discharged from the military as a disabled person.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: In what way was he disabled?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Well, he got sick in the military. How can I know? Why are you bothering me with all of this now?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, were all the people in that room older and of not good health?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Everybody was old and weak and worn out, good for nothing; useless.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Sir, how long were you detained at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I stayed until the 15th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about your release. Before you were released, were you ever called to a meeting or called to somebody's office?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. No. I don't remember any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know -- could you tell us the circumstances of your release? Who arranged your release?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: We didn't dare ask anything or say anything. We only dare do what we were ordered to do. The three of us received orders and two shifts left. Thirty people were exchanged. That was one group, and on the 15th [Realtime transcript read in error"309"] of December 13 people left. All of them were young and they said goodbye to us. There were some whom I knew and they have been missing until the present day. Then after that, they called us out. We got into a vehicle and went all the way to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Until now, I was hesitant to react. I thought that I would correct the transcript through the cross-examination. However, there is a number 309 on the 13th page, line 11, and that number is wrong, 309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it's probably the 30th of December, isn't it, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. rather than 309. It may be a typographical error rather than a translation error. Ms. Kuo, do you remember the answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think the best thing to say, Mr. Bakrac, is that when the transcript is checked this afternoon, they'll pay special attention to that. Did you hear the witness say "309"?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's why I did react, because the witness did not say "309" and the transcript says "309". So that was the point of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that will be checked --

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I did not say "309".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That sorts it out. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps I should go back through that portion because there is a lot of information that needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Mr. Cengic, you said that there were two shifts and you mentioned December. Can you tell us when the first of the two shifts that you mentioned occurred, when the first group of people were taken out that you know of?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I can't say. The first exchange was in December. As for the 15th of December, there are some people I knew there, and they came to say goodbye to me and that's why I remember that. And until the present day, they've been missing, and then people ask me about them too and then I tell them such-and-such a thing were happened. They were taken out for an exchange, and what I could do there? I didn't dare ask anything or say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of anybody taken out on that exchange on the 15th of December?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I do. There was Ekrem Cengic from Ustikolina, from Cvilin. There was Malkic. I don't know his name exactly. Then there was Lagarija. I don't know what his name was really. He's from Sutjeska. And then also some others that I knew. I can't remember their names now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And you said people have asked you what happened to them. You have never heard from them again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "The answer was inaudible," says the witness.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: People are -- people are being looked for, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you know Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No, honestly I didn't. Honestly, I didn't, and I don't know him. I had nothing to do with him ever, nor did I ever meet him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know Marko Kovac?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Marko Kovac? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you said you were taken to Belgrade, how were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: A vehicle came. They said, "Off you go." We got ready, and we went. They probably got orders from someone too. How should I know?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How many people were released with you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Only three of us left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who left with you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Fehim and Hilmo. Fehim died in Tetovo. And Hilmo is alive. I don't know where he is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And Fehim and Hilmo were also related and also named Cengic, right?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you learn later how your exchange or your release had been arranged? Did somebody on the outside make arrangements for you to be released, such as a family member?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Family members? Of course my children had to look for me and wonder where I was, but nobody told me anything. They just said to me, "Get ready," and then they took us to Belgrade. We didn't even know we were going to Belgrade until we got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: While you were in the KP Dom, did you ever receive treatment for the injuries that you received at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Nobody treated me, and I didn't even go out to eat. If they brought something to me to eat, I ate. And I didn't even go to the toilet for 20 days. I couldn't pass a stool. That's the way the food was. And nobody really did anything to me. So that's what it was like while I was at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. Those are the questions of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall try to be even briefer than my learned colleague was. The Defence has two questions. Although we believe that the tape will be checked, we are just going to go back to some questions that we believe were not entered into the transcript. I didn't want to interrupt my learned friend, and I understand all the technical problems that happen, but I'll be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Bakrac please not speak at the time the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: I had an operation a month ago. Please bear that in mind. I am quite, you know, desperate, and I am really not up to a lot of interrogation or whatever. If you can be as short as possible, because I've got to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the interpreters said that on that occasion you were actually asking a question while the witness was still speaking, Not just the interpretation but while the witness himself was speaking. So please try to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with due respect to the interpreters, the witness started speaking while I was still speaking, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I have full respect for your age and your health, and believe me, I'll try to be much briefer than we usually have been during these examinations. I'm just going to put a few questions to you. I am Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney-at-law, one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Krnojelac. Sir, you said that you had two sons in Sarajevo. Can you tell me what they did at the time when the conflict broke out in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: They were engineers. They did their own work. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did they stay in Sarajevo throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. One stayed throughout the war and the other one went out to take care of his wife and children, and of the others too, so -- of the other one, too, so he stayed in [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Muhamed Cengic?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is he related to you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Related? My brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are we talking about Muhamed Cengic, a high official of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Is that what he was? You mean a leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I did not hear your answer, sir. I don't know what you said. Are we talking about a high leader of the SDA, Muhamed Cengic?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are talking about him. He was a leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: However, during the time, he was a high official of the SDA, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was, and then he went to [redacted], and then he never returned until the war ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You talked about villages, Mrdjanovici, Izbisno, Govza 1, Govza 2. What is the ethnic composition of these villages or what was the ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Mostly Muslims. In Govza there were some Serbs. In the other three there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about Mrdjanovici; there were no Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about Izbisno?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: No. At Poljice there were some Serbs, but there were more Muslims anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You talked about the 17th of August, 1992. I would just like to clarify something. You said today during the examination-in-chief that a policeman came to arrest you, and in your statement you said that a Serb soldier came.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: It's all the same to me. It's not a policeman who came, it's a soldier who came. Not one; five or six of them. They came in a car. They rounded us up and took us to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You have said something already. I please -- I hope you won't mind that we have to repeat this, but we need something here in the transcript. You mentioned Dr. Milena Begenisic. Is it correct that you said that she took care of you as if she were your mother or sister?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Even better than that. I cannot express her -- appreciation to her in any other way. No one was better to me in my life. Not my mother nor my sister. When I could not speak, she made me come to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you said that this soldier who threatened to slit your throat, when she called the police said that he would slit her throat too?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: He said so immediately, that he'd slit her throat too, and that is why she called the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did she stay with you until late at night?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: She stayed until she sent us off to the KP Dom. However, I did not see -- she sent me this letter of discharge from the hospital, and that's why I say that she got us ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that you also said that you were sent to the KP Dom so that you would not see your end in the hospital because of such persons?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: We were told that we had to go to the KP Dom because there is no security in the hospital, that he would come and that he would slit our throats and that's why they got us ready and dispatched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you talked about Mr. Hilmo or Fehim Cengic, you said that he could not see 9 per cent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Five per cent, not 9 per cent. He could not see 5 per cent. That's what he had a piece of paper saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And he was born with that defect?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was born with that kind of defect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is it also correct that you were brought to the KP Dom on the 2nd of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: On the 2nd of October? I did not say that. I think it was in September that I came to the KP Dom. I was in hospital for 50 days, and on the 17th of August, I was deprived of my liberty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I'll just try to refresh your memory. I'm going to read from a statement that you gave in 1995 to the OTP: On the 2nd of October, 1992, a tall Chetnik in SMB uniform came and said that he heard that there were some Ustashes in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that on the 2nd -- that after the 2nd of October, after this tall Chetnik, as you said, came, you went to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: That night we went. The lady doctor got us ready. She asked the municipality to send a vehicle to the KP Dom to transfer us and that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, my last question, I'm not going to trouble you any more: You talked about the exchange in December, and in your statement given in 1995, you mentioned that, in this group, there was also Malkic and a Slovenian journalist. You did not mention the names of Lagarija and Cengic, the ones you mentioned today. How come your memory of these names is better today than it was in 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: They didn't ask me. Since this question was put to me, I remember these people who came to cover me with a blanket, and I was so weak, and I wanted to die. It was so cold and there was no heating in the room and there was no food, and that's the way it was. There was Lagarija, Malkic, Cengic. I knew them. And perhaps I said -- I don't know what I said when they asked me. I don't know. And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, you said you were taken with Hilmo and Fehim Cengic by car to Belgrade. Who drove you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: A driver. A driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. He wore an English [as interpreted] kind of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So he wore a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was this uniform that was worn by other soldiers at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, you said that you wouldn't be asking me too many questions. You are interested in uniforms and I'm interested in my life. For ten years now I've been bothered by all these questions and everything and I was not interested in this uniform, and now if you're interested, what can I tell you? I don't know and I can't tell you. I don't know and I'm not going to lie either. So there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: There's a mistake in the transcript. That is why I wanted to clarify this and this is indeed my last question, sir: In the KP Dom, did you have a male nurse named Gojko Jokanovic coming to see you?

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: A man came - they say he was there before - and he gave some pills out. He didn't give anything to me, and I didn't ask for any, and what could he give me, anyway?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: NEZIR CENGIC
utterances.text: Oh, thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You are now free to leave. Thank you for giving evidence before the Tribunal. Now, do we go back to the witness we were on yesterday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's Witness 89.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. We had asked for him to be brought in. We thought that we would take this first hour and a half break. We've contacted the Victims and Witnesses Unit and they haven't gotten back to us, so I'm afraid he won't be available until 12.00. We didn't want to keep him waiting in the morning; we prefer to have him in the hotel so he wouldn't be very anxious when he came into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't know where you must have kept him yesterday if you're worried about him being anxious, Ms. Kuo. Anyway, if he's not here, he's not here. Perhaps could you have an inquiry made before we go off for an hour to see whether somebody could speak -- whether your case manager can speak to somebody downstairs. Perhaps while we are waiting, I might make an inquiry. Has something been sorted out about the medical examination yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday, at least yesterday at lunchtime, our expert hadn't got the report, but we have provided the e-mail address and her correct fax number to Defence counsel. Now, if she received it today, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, may I address you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have contacted our expert. Our expert confirmed that she sent her expert opinion last Thursday, Ms. Najman to Ms. Forlegovic, and Ms. Forlegovic said that she would complete her expert opinion by Thursday, by tomorrow, and then they would send that to the OTP. That's the information I have as of last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've been told that the Victims and Witnesses Unit is sending somebody to the courtroom to let us know whether they've located the witness and, if so, how much time it will require to bring him in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We will adjourn and somebody can let us know when we're expected back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Are you feeling better today?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: At the end of the day yesterday we were talking about -- I had asked you whether you had seen Mr. Krnojelac, and you said that you did see him when you were chopping wood and cutting grass and collecting hay. Could you tell us what Mr. Krnojelac was doing when you saw him on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came on inspection tours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to him or did he talk to the people who were working?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us to take care, not to get hurt, to take care.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: These places where you were chopping wood and cutting grass and collecting hay, where were they? Were they far from the farm?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a place from Brod, near Kopilovi, a hillock just beyond there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you ever paid for the work that you did while you were at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't pay us for the work that we did. We only got cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you ever charged with a crime while you were detained at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you ever given the opportunity to ask to be released?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To ask to be released? No. I didn't even ask. I didn't even try to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you were taken outside to work, did townspeople ever provoke you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one incident when we were working at the mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened during that incident?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened when we left for work at 7.00 a.m. The car broke down in town, and we weren't able to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did the townspeople do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individuals among them asked us to take off our caps. They wanted to take them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there anything special about those caps?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the caps that had been distributed to us by the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And was it to keep warm because it was winter?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did the townspeople point any weapons at you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What town was this in when this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened in town, near the post office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: In Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there another occasion when someone slapped you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was an incident when I was working at the bakery, unloading flour. A young man by the name of Slobo Curcic slapped me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there a guard present?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did the guard react?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard ran up to us, and he told me -- he told him not to touch me, but the young man had already slapped me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When were you finally released from KP Dom? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Finally it was on the 10th of May, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10th of May. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we were let out that day, they escorted us on a bus to Kula, and there was an incident wherein two young men came up -- came through the door, pointed guns at us, and told the driver to drive us back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, were you released with the last group of detainees at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And had you previously told the Office of the Prosecution that it was the 5th of October, 1994, when you were released? That is, the fifth day of the tenth month.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Today you said it was the tenth day of the fifth month. Was that a mistake today?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were you released in October?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in October. On the 5th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I am lawyer Mihajlo Bakrac, one of the Defence counsel of the accused Milorad Krnojelac. I will ask you a couple of questions, but I would kindly ask you that when I ask you a question, please make a pause for the interpretation to finish and only then answer me.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief, sir, you said that on the 8th of April, the war in Foca began; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also true that in your statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor, you said that shooting began at 9.30?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief yesterday, you said that on the 8th of April, you went to work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When? At what time after you went to work did you go to the bank?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was unable to work; we were turned back from the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And after that, you went to the bank?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where is that bank?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How far is your enterprise from the place where you resided?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten or 15, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And how far is your Ljubovic - that is, the house of your cousin in Ljubovic - from the place where you worked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is closer when you go across the Cehotina. Perhaps ten minutes away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you claim that the house of your cousin in Ljubovic is closer to the place where you worked than your apartment?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How -- at what time were you at the bank?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was after noon, after 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mean at noon?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was supposed to work the second shift, starting at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Your wife and your three children remained at your apartment; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, two children and my wife. My third daughter was in Sarajevo at school.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You have just told us that on the 8th, in the morning, shooting started in town around 9.30, and around 12.00 you went to the bank, and yesterday you told us that you didn't go home but instead you went to your cousin's house because you were unable, due to the shooting, to go to your home.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did you leave your home?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the cousin's home?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, your home.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, when I went to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Meaning after the shooting had begun? Can you answer me? Is it after the shooting had begun? You said the shooting began at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said you were working the second shift. You left your flat, you left your two children and wife behind, and -- after the shooting had begun. And here, during the examination, you said you couldn't come back home because there was shooting around.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the second day, on another day, because that evening I spent the night at my cousin's, and that was the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You told us it was on the 8th of April when the shooting began at 9.30, and you said yesterday and you confirmed today that on the 8th of April, you went to work and you went to the bank.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went to my cousin's that evening. I spent the night there and that happened in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why did you spend the night at your cousin's, having left your wife and children at your apartment?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there just to see them, see how they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know where the driver Karasi's house is in Ljubovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where was the mortar installed on the Karasi house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see. I didn't enter his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know there was a mortar on the Karasi house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see it. I was at his brother's house. That was the house next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mean you were in the next house to his where the mortar was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see any mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To whom did you turn over your weapon?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: None of the 15 people with whom you were had any weapons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any weapons. I know about myself. Personally I didn't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about the others? Do you know whether they had weapons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Others had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You were the only one who didn't?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did the others have?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His brother had some kind of device, some rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you say in your statement that Muslims had to turn over their weapons when the war had been lost?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said that it would be better to turn over the weapons, that no one would suffer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were the weapons turned over?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people did turn over their weapons; others didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Those who didn't, what did they do with it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They must have kept them for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you turn over some weapons to Bozo Dostic, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any weapons at all. I didn't carry any. I didn't possess any, and I didn't carry any.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How come that Bozo Dostic turned up at your place and was in charge of 15 or 16 Muslims who were at the Karasi house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't at the Karasi house, we were at Avdo Muratovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That is next door to the Karasi house?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you hear shooting around?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please tell me, sir, yesterday you spoke about this, I just want to clarify something you said in your statement. When you asked Dostic to allow you to go to see your wife and children, he told you that he had to ask Boro Ivanovic, the commander. Was he a military commander?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he was. He must have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm asking you because in your statement, you said, "He said he would ask Boro Ivanovic, who was the Serbian military commander." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You also said in your statement that KP Dom was guarded by soldiers wearing blue uniforms --

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- when you came to the KP Dom. I want to know what that means. Were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those were guards who had worked even before, while there was freedom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you used to see soldiers there as well?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You told us yesterday, sir, that on that day when you were brought to the KP Dom, you were taken to Room 12. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That after 20 days, you were transferred to Room 16.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that, in Room 16, you stayed until July 1993?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And then after July 1993, you spent several days in Room 20?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And after that, you spent all the rest of the time, until your release, in Room 13?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you give us a drawing of the rooms where you were detained, to the Office of the Prosecutor, indicating where those rooms were located?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those rooms are located --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. I didn't ask you where they were located. We'll try to clear that up in a different way. I only want to know whether you had made a drawing of the KP Dom, the prisoners' quarters, buildings 1 and 2, and indicated exactly where those rooms were located?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like the drawing that you made put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask to have this redacted, or at least have the ELMO placed so that the name is not visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just take it off the ELMO. Take it off the ELMO. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I didn't pay attention and didn't see the name on the bottom. I would have reacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's all right, Mr. Bakrac. It's taken care of now. We can redact the whole of that time that it was on the ELMO. Put it back, would you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, please be so kind as to show me on the drawing that you made where is Room 12? Where are the windows of the Room 12 where you were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here on the drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the transcript, the witness is indicating building number 1, the first and second windows on the left-hand side, circled, and below there is an inscription "Room 12." You have just indicated, sir, Room 13. Where was Room 12? Can you show us Room 12 on this drawing? Sir, can you indicate to us the location of Room 16?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe it would be a better idea for the usher to take the photograph of these two buildings so that the witness can indicate it to us on the photograph. Perhaps the drawing is confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, I'll give you a photograph. Please try to show this to us on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The photograph is 7512.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was just going to identify the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We can start from the building marked with number "2" in a yellow circle. Where is Room 16?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness any longer.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 16 was on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You are showing the warehouse, the cellar.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then this is Room 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You are indicating windows on the ground floor. What were the windows of your room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were four windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The windows you are indicating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the benefit of the transcript, the witness is indicating that he was in Room 16, on the ground floor, and that this room included all the four windows in front which are visible. So this is the annex building, the part of the building marked by number "2" in a yellow circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you agree with that description, Ms. Kuo?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please show me now where was Room 20.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 20 was on the upper floor, upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating the four windows on the second floor, above the ground floor, the four windows located above Room 16 in the same annex building marked with number "2" in a yellow circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell me now, Witness, looking at this photograph, where were Room 12 and 13?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rooms 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which room are you indicating now?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This room. This room. This was 11 and -- that was the ground floor, and 13 was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is 13 upstairs in that part that you are indicating or the part where it says number "1" in a circle?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number "1".

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That's Room 13; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating the window on the second floor in the annex building above which there is number "1" in a circle. The witness indicated the first window on the right-hand side -- the first window on the left-hand side - I'm sorry - the one facing annex number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not going to trouble you with this any more. Just tell me, is Room 12 in the same building, building number 1, where Room 13 is?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same entrance, except that you enter on the right-hand side for Room 12, whereas Room 13 to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And the windows of Room 12, where you were, also face the compound of the KP Dom and the administration building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the usher. We no longer need this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you were in these rooms with the work platoon. Was a person named Safet Avdic with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Safet Avdic was not in my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there another work platoon, another work room or was it only your room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another work room where the metalworkers were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where were they? In which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The room behind my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you were in four rooms, so we don't know exactly in which room they were.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in 13, and they were behind my room, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that Room 14?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, Witness, that in your statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor, you said the following: "Zoran Vladicic and another soldier were investigators at the KP Dom." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to clarify another matter. As I checked some of the shifts of various working days, yesterday it was not quite clear in your examination-in-chief, is it true that you started working in the mine in Miljevina in September or October 1993 for the first time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And that you worked there until March 1994?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I worked there for six months. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you in the group of miners who worked in the Miljevina mine?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was, for six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was this the first group that went to work in Miljevina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Yesterday, you talked about certain persons about whom you had heard that they were taken out to go plum picking. Is it correct that you stated to the Office of the Prosecutor the following: This is page number 8, the third paragraph, these are two sentences. I'll read them slowly: "Once in the KP Dom, 36 prisoners were singled out to go and pick plums. I was not there at the time because I was working at the farm at Brioni." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you remember which year this was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The year was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you remember the month?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The month was September.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you heard about this from the other detainees. Did you hear about that when you got out of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Yesterday, in the -- actually, in the statement you gave to the OTP, you gave almost 20 names. Yesterday you could not remember a single one. Did they tell you then the names of the persons who were taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People talked about it, but some do not know all the people, and I don't know all of them by name. Quite a bit of time has gone by. I can't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. remember how many years; six, seven. I've forgotten. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You said yesterday that you worked on heating the KP Dom. When was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the month of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the month of May 1992. What were you doing in respect of heating?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were stoking furnaces for the kitchen, putting coal in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know that the central heating at the KP Dom had been destroyed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I tell you? In the rooms where we were, there was no heating. This was only for the kitchen and for baths.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For baths where?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For baths down there in the bathrooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did detainees bathe there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was firewood used for cooking in the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firewood was used later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At the time when you were brought to the KP Dom and after that, were there brownouts often at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few times when there was no electricity at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, did you state that there was no central heating at the KP Dom during your first year there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is the reason for that precisely the breakdown in the system of heating, the mechanical breakdown that we mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, and it is also possible that there were not sufficient resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the so-called day room of your detainee room, did you have a furnace?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a furnace in 1993, when the Red Cross registered us. We had furnaces with firewood and coal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you stated that, during the winter, they gave you additional blankets?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How many blankets did you get?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had four blankets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. When the Red Cross gave these furnaces, did they give them to the detainees in the various detainee rooms?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Yesterday, you talked about working on a farm. Now we heard that in September 1992, when 36 people were taken out, that you were at the farm at Brioni. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that, at the farm, eggs, milk, and meat were produced. Did detainees get any of that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday, I had the impression that you had stopped at a point when you said that they got eggs. Did they also get milk and meat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We got eggs and meat and milk, we who were engaged in physical labour, who were more exposed to physical labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did the other detainees get that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the others didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Not at all or not as much as you got?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I don't know what "yes" means. Is it not as much as you who worked there got or --

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not get as much as we got. They got smaller quantities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said yesterday that part of this produce went to civilians in Foca in addition to going to the detainees.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know that part of this produce also went to the military?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You worked at the farm. I'm asking you whether you know that the military took some of this with them, rather, some of this produce.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked up there and then we sent that to town, and who took all of that, I don't know, I can't tell you for sure. Somebody must have used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the basis of what do you infer that Muslims could not buy this produce unless Serb neighbours gave it to them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't because they probably didn't have the money to buy it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that your assumption?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, actually -- I'm sorry. Is it correct that you said in your statement you gave to the OTP that Dr. Aziz Torlak was taken away from the KP Dom in 1994?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was there until the very last -- how should I put this? He was the last to be taken out of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which month was this? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the month of June maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. A few minutes ago when my learned friend was questioning you, you talked about the incidents concerning caps which occurred in Foca. Was this in the period when you worked at the mine in Miljevina?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So that happened between September 1993 and perhaps March 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you stated to the office of the OTP that your wife and children sought permission to leave Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did they seek such permission several times?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: They -- when they finally got this permission, they finally left Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They left Foca on the 19th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mean the 19th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-89 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these were all the questions of the Defence. We have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Kuo, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That concludes your evidence. We are grateful to you for having come to the Tribunal to give it. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, 137 is the next one, is that so? And the protective measures at the moment are the usual, facial distortion and pseudonym; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is it a voice distortion? No?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, the pseudonym sheet for 137 will be Exhibit P443, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Witness, would you please make the declaration in the document that is being shown to you by the court usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
