We are very interested in what you want to say about the issues we have to determine. We understand, too, that this is your first trial. It's the first trial for most people where you have these translation problems. There are problems which are necessary, because we don't speak your language, and we have to have your evidence translated into either English or French, and it does take time for the translation. That's why I explained it to you. We are not criticising you. We are just trying to help you to help us so we hear your evidence. Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Witness, with the assistance of the usher, I would like you to take a look at the first pages of these statements so that you could tell us whether this is your signature on the bottom of these pages. It is statements ID 252, 253, and 251. If you've had a look, tell us whether these your statements that you read and signed in your own hand.

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: If I can see this properly, these are my signatures. But as for the statements, whether they match, well the signature is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you read these statements before you signed them? You signed them on every page.

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: I don't remember that I read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these statements read out to you by the persons who took them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: I swear -- I swear by my mother, and you know what a mother is, that I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. When you gave statements to these authorities, did you give your personal details?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: I had to give my personal details when they asked me for them, and I did do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Were these personal details entered into the statements that you signed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: I don't know about that, about what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to ask for a private session, to go into private session just for a short while, just for a few questions, because they relate to the witness's personal details, and if we would not going into private session, then the public would become aware of his details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's all right, but is there some challenge to his signature on the document? Nobody has suggested that it's not his document. If you really need it, we'll certainly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall explain, Your Honour. I'm not bringing into question or challenging the signature on the document. I would like the witness to explain to me some of the details that he gave when he made this statement. They are relevant to him. However, they differ in respect of what he said today.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You mean apart from the spelling of his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can be of assistance. When you look at the list, the sheet of paper, I put in brackets after the date of birth the date of birth in the passport, because in the various statements, it's always a different date more or less. Therefore, I looked into the passport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Anyway, how do you know that was correct? We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, in which rooms were you during your stay at the KP Dom and for what period of time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: I was in number 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please, sir, you just have to pause. Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you hear the question? In which rooms were you during your stay at the KP Dom and during which period of time? Just let the interpreters finish and then start answering, please.

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: I was in Room 11 from the month of April until the month of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: And from the month of July until the day of your exchange, in which room were you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: In -- from July, I was transferred to Room 18, upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Until when were you in Room 18?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: Until, I think, the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Until when were you in Room 18?

utterances.speaker: FWS-137
utterances.text: Until sometime in November 1992. Sometime in November 1992, I went to Kalinovik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we'll have it set up in the morning so that the witness will have the transcript in front of him and he can see when the typing finishes, but it's hardly worth trying to fix it up this afternoon. Otherwise, I'm afraid, we'll never have a clean interpretation. We will adjourn now. 9.30 tomorrow. We're back to normal sitting hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 29th day of March, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.28 p.m.,
